newsitem.title: USA: Wolverine shares tumble on weak earnings.
newsitem.headline: Wolverine shares tumble on weak earnings.

text.p: Shares of Wolverine Tube fell nearly 25 percent on Tuesday after the company on Monday said it expected weak first-quarter profits.
But analysts differed over the long-term prospects for the Huntsville, Ala.-based copper tube maker.

Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Martin Sankey cut his rating on the stock to hold from buy, but Harriet Baldwin at Lehman Brothers said she is maintaining her buy rating, with an 18-month price target of 46.
"The company has some problems, but I think they are well positioned for the long term," said Baldwin in an interview.

Baldwin did cut her 1997 earnings estimate to $2.85 per share from an earlier $3.60 estimate but said her 1998 estimate of $3.30, at a price to earnings ratio of 14, supports the 18-month target price.

"The market has reacted to the earnings disappointment at Wolverine Tube as it has to disappointments at other companies. But the stock still offers an attractive opportunity for longer-term investors," Baldwin added.
Wolverine shares were down 8-5/8 at 26-3/8 on volume of 555,700 in late morning trade.
In a statement released after the closing bell on Monday, Wolverine said it expected first-quarter profit to be 15 percent below first-quarter 1996 earnings of $0.72 per share.
Analysts had been expecting Wolverine to earn $0.88 per share, according to First Call's consensus of analysts.
